rationale: The hypothesis posits that severe congenital microcephaly and major structural congenital heart disease are typically absent in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder and that their presence strongly argues against the diagnosis. However, clinical and genetic reports in the literature contradict this claim. Microcephaly is an established feature of severe DHX9-related phenotypes (specifically those harboring nuclear localization signal missense variants or group 2 severe neurodevelopmental disorders, as well as curated on Genomics England PanelApp). Furthermore, cardiac defects, including ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy and cardiac arrhythmias/cardiac concerns, have been documented in individuals harboring pathogenic de novo DHX9 variants.

evidence.text: In a study describing 20 individuals with de novo DHX9 variants, individuals with nuclear localization signal missense variants exhibited severe neurodevelopmental disorder phenotypes characterized by microcephaly and structural brain abnormalities, whereas mild/LoF cases lacked microcephaly.

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts that severe congenital microcephaly and major congenital heart disease are typically absent and argue against DHX9-related disorder, whereas published cohorts identify microcephaly in severe/NLS missense groups and document structural cardiomyopathy (ventricular non-compaction) and arrhythmias.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and spectrum of congenital cardiac anomalies (including cardiomyopathy and conduction abnormalities) in expanded DHX9 cohorts stratified by variant domain?
new_directions.rationale: Reports have identified ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy and cardiac arrhythmias in specific missense variants, but broader cohort data are required to establish systematic screening guidelines.

new_directions.question_text: Does microcephaly in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder strictly correlate with nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense variants leading to cytoplasmic accumulation, versus loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: Calame et al. observed genotype-phenotype divergence where group 1 LoF variants lacked microcephaly while severe NLS missense variants caused microcephaly; verifying this across all known cases will refine genotype-guided prognostic counseling.
